newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Six Swazis shot by police in eight day stayaway.
newsitem.headline: Six Swazis shot by police in eight day stayaway.

text.p: Six striking sugar plantation workers were wounded on Tuesday when Swaziland police opened fire on a crowd of about 3,000 protesters near Big Bend, a private security official said.

"Six people were taken to hospital with gunshot wounds, five of them were workers from Ubombo Ranches, one of the three biggest sugar estates in Swaziland," a security official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
He said the workers were gathered near the main road leading from South Africa to Manzini, the industrial capital of the tiny landlocked kingdom, when they were approached by police.
"It is our understanding that the police were not in a life-threatening situation," he said, but declined to elaborate.
Five of the six people had gunshot wounds below the abdomen, he said.

The situation on the Ubombo Ranches was tense but police had been persuaded to leave the area overnight, he said, adding that a meeting would be held on Wednesday between the union, ranch managers and police to discuss the incident.
Police and union official were not immediately available for commment.

A national strike was called eight days ago by the Swaziland Federation of Trade Unions to push for a speeding up of democratic change in the kingdom after a 1973 royal decree vested all state powers in the monarch and banned political activity.
The sugar and timber industries, Swaziland's biggest foreign exchange earners, have been hardest hit by the stayaway and are losing millions of dollars.

Unions are also demanding the release of four union leaders who were arrested at the beginning of the strike and charged with violating public order. They will appear in an Mbabane court next Wednesday to face charges.
